note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Raise an alert when an account makes more than 5 card payments within any 10 minute period. Return the time of the payment that caused the alert. Payments exactly 10 minutes apart are in different periods.
facts: Input is a list of payment times in order, in UTC. Made-up example: payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08, 10:09 alert at 10:09. Payments at 10:00 and 10:10 are not in the same period.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Input is one account's card payment times as a list, in time order, in UTC.
REQ-2: Two payments are in the same 10 minute period only if the later one is less than 10 minutes after the earlier one. Payments exactly 10 minutes apart are in different periods.
REQ-3: Raise an alert when a payment brings the number of payments in one period to more than 5, meaning it is the 6th payment within that period.
REQ-4: The alert returns the UTC time of the payment that caused it. If no payment does this, no alert is raised. Open question for the requester: the brief does not say whether payments after the first alert can raise further alerts.
AC-1: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08 and 10:09 raise an alert at 10:09. This is 6 payments, and 10:09 is 9 minutes after 10:00.
AC-2: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08 and 10:10 raise no alert. 10:10 is exactly 10 minutes after 10:00, so that period holds only 10:02 to 10:10, which is 5 payments.
AC-3: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06 and 10:08 raise no alert. This is only 5 payments.
AC-4: Payments at 10:00 and 10:10 are treated as being in different periods.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: Input is an ordered list of card payment times in UTC for an account.
REQ-2: Raise an alert when the account makes more than 5 card payments within any 10 minute period.
REQ-3: Payments exactly 10 minutes apart are in different periods.
REQ-4: Return the time of the payment that caused the alert.
AC-1: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08, 10:09 alert at 10:09.
AC-2: Payments at 10:00 and 10:10 are not in the same period.

reviewOfA.strengths: The draft keeps the alert at more than 5 payments, treats a span of exactly 10 minutes as a different period, and matches the given alert at 10:09.

findings.title: Repeat and no-alert behaviour undefined
findings.detail: The requirements do not say whether only the first triggering payment is returned or every later payment in the same window also alerts, nor what is returned when no alert occurs. These are open questions for the visitor, not facts to invent, but they should be resolved before approval.
findings.quote: REQ-4: Return the time of the payment that caused the alert.

findings.title: AC-2 lacks observable outcome
findings.detail: AC-2 restates the boundary rule but gives no expected system result, so it cannot be tested directly. It could be tied to an alert or no-alert outcome, using only the stated facts, for example by building a case on the AC-1 sequence.
findings.quote: AC-2: Payments at 10:00 and 10:10 are not in the same period.

reviewOfB.strengths: The draft restates the threshold (more than 5), the 10 minute window, the exclusive boundary and the AC-1 example exactly as given; six payments from 10:00 to 10:09 correctly fall within 10 minutes and alert at 10:09.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Input is one account's card payment times as a list, in time order, in UTC.
REQ-2: Two payments are in the same 10 minute period only if the later one is less than 10 minutes after the earlier one. Payments exactly 10 minutes apart are in different periods.
REQ-3: Raise an alert when a payment brings the number of payments in one period to more than 5, meaning it is the 6th payment within that period.
REQ-4: The alert returns the UTC time of the payment that caused it. If no payment does this, no alert is raised.
Open question for the requester: the brief does not say whether payments after the first alert, in the same or a later period, raise further alerts. This must be answered before approval.
AC-1: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08 and 10:09 raise an alert at 10:09. This is 6 payments, and 10:09 is 9 minutes after 10:00.
AC-2: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08 and 10:10 raise no alert. 10:10 is exactly 10 minutes after 10:00, so they are in different periods. The period ending at 10:10 holds only 10:02 to 10:10, which is 5 payments.
AC-3: Payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06 and 10:08 raise no alert. This is only 5 payments.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure and wording, including the precise period rule, the 6th-payment threshold, the no-alert statement, the open question and its worked acceptance criteria. I checked each criterion's numbers.
merge.keptFromB: From draft B I kept the point raised in its review that repeat-alert behaviour must be settled before approval. I also kept the rule that every acceptance criterion must state a testable outcome, so A's untestable AC-4 boundary restatement became part of AC-2.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 · P1 · Repeat and no-alert behaviour undefined
resolutions.note: REQ-4 states that no alert is raised when no payment makes a 6th in one period. Whether later payments raise further alerts is recorded as an open question for the requester rather than invented, and it must be answered before approval.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 · P2 · AC-2 lacks observable outcome
resolutions.note: B's AC-2 and A's matching AC-4 are replaced by a testable case built on the AC-1 sequence. With 10:10 in place of 10:09 the expected result is no alert, because 10:00 and 10:10 are in different periods and the period ending at 10:10 holds only 5 payments.

finalReview.strengths: The acceptance criteria correctly recompute the six-payment alert at 10:09 and the exact ten-minute boundary that produces no alert.

build.contract: checkCardPayments(input) where input = { paymentTimes } (an array of strings, each a UTC time in ISO 8601 form such as "2024-01-01T10:09:00Z", for one account, in time order). Returns { alert: boolean, alertTime: string or null (the UTC time of the payment that caused the alert, in the same ISO 8601 form as the input; null when alert is false) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field. This shape reports at most one alert. If the requester's answer to the open question is that later payments raise further alerts, alertTime becomes alertTimes: string[] (empty when there is no alert) before the contract is approved.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function, checkCardPayments(input), with no I/O, no clock and no stored state. It works on one account's list per call.
Validation: reject any field other than paymentTimes with Error("unknown field: <name>"). The brief does not cover malformed times, unordered lists or a missing paymentTimes, so do not add rules for them; raise these with the requester.
Data: parse each ISO 8601 UTC string to epoch milliseconds once. Keep the original strings so alertTime is returned exactly as given.
Core logic: a sliding window with two indexes (left, i). For each payment i, advance left while time[i] - time[left] >= 600000 ms, so payments exactly 10 minutes apart fall out of the window (REQ-2).
Alert: when i - left + 1 > 5, which is the 6th payment in the period, return { alert: true, alertTime: paymentTimes[i] } (REQ-3, REQ-4). If the loop ends with no alert, return { alert: false, alertTime: null }.
The function stops at the first alert. This matches the current contract, which reports at most one alert. The open question about further alerts blocks approval. If the answer is yes, keep scanning without resetting and collect the times into alertTimes; the same files change.
Cost: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, because each index moves forward only.
Tests: AC-1 alerts at 10:09. AC-2 gives no alert, since the 10:10 window holds only 10:02 to 10:10, which is 5 payments. AC-3 gives no alert with 5 payments. Also test that an unknown field throws and that an empty list gives no alert.
File fence (proposed names, because the repo layout is not given): new src/checkCardPayments.js and new test/checkCardPayments.test.js. No other files may change.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: The window drops a payment when the gap is 600000 ms or more, so times exactly 10 minutes apart are not in the same period, matching REQ-2 and AC-2.
architecture.final:

Validation: reject any field other than paymentTimes with Error("unknown field: <name>"). The brief does not cover malformed times, unordered lists or a missing paymentTimes, so add no rules for them and raise them with the requester.
Data: parse each ISO 8601 UTC string to epoch milliseconds once. Keep the original strings so alertTime is returned exactly as given.
Core logic: a sliding window with two indexes, left and i. For each payment i, advance left while time[i] - time[left] >= 600000 ms, so payments exactly 10 minutes apart fall out of the window (REQ-2).
Alert: when i - left + 1 > 5, which is the 6th payment in the period, return { alert: true, alertTime: paymentTimes[i] } (REQ-3, REQ-4). If the loop ends with no alert, return { alert: false, alertTime: null }.
The function stops at the first alert, which matches the current contract. The open question about further alerts blocks approval. If the answer is yes, keep scanning without resetting and collect the times into alertTimes, changing the same files.
Cost: O(n) time, because each index only moves forward. Extra space is O(n) for the parsed times; this corrects the earlier O(1) claim.

architecture.resolutions: Self-check: Cost line claimed O(1) extra space although every time is parsed into an array of epoch milliseconds applied: Changed to O(n) extra space for the parsed times. The review raised no findings; this correction came from checking the numbers.

code.summary: Pure function checkCardPayments({ paymentTimes }). It throws "unknown field: <name>" for any field other than paymentTimes. Each ISO 8601 UTC string is parsed to epoch milliseconds once, and the original strings are kept. A two-index sliding window moves left forward while time[i] - time[left] >= 600000 ms, so payments exactly 10 minutes apart fall in different periods (REQ-2). It returns { alert: true, alertTime: paymentTimes[i] } at the first point where the window holds more than 5 payments (REQ-3, REQ-4). Otherwise it returns { alert: false, alertTime: null }. Behaviour checked by hand: AC-1 (10:00 to 10:08 and 10:09) alerts at 10:09, the 6th payment within 9 minutes. AC-2 (ending at 10:10) gives no alert: 10:00 leaves the window, so 10:02 to 10:10 is 5 payments. AC-3 (5 payments) gives no alert. An empty list gives no alert. Cost is O(n) time and O(n) space. Malformed times, unordered lists and a missing paymentTimes are not handled and stay with the requester, as the architecture says. The open question still blocks approval: does a payment after the first alert raise another alert? This code stops at the first alert, which fits the current contract. If the answer is yes, the contract changes to alertTimes: string[] and the loop keeps scanning without resetting.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: The sliding window treats a span of exactly 10 minutes as outside the period and alerts on the sixth payment, matching AC-1, AC-2, and the single-alert contract.
code.resolutions: No defects found; the sliding window excludes payments exactly 10 minutes apart and alerts on the sixth payment, matching AC-1, AC-2 and the single-alert contract. applied: Agreed after my own check, so the code is unchanged. AC-1: at 10:09 the gap to 10:00 is 9 minutes, under 600000 ms. The window holds 6 payments, so the alert returns 10:09. AC-2: at 10:10 the gap to 10:00 is exactly 600000 ms, so 10:00 drops out. The window holds 5 payments and no alert is raised. AC-3: only 5 payments, so no alert is raised. Any field other than paymentTimes throws 'unknown field: <name>'. The function returns at the first alert, which fits the at-most-one-alert shape. The open question about further alerts is still unresolved.

diagram.summary: An outside calling system sends one account's ordered UTC payment times to a new pure function in src/checkCardPayments.js; the function rejects unknown fields, parses the times to milliseconds, then runs a sliding 10 minute window and returns the time of the 6th payment in a period, or no alert.
